_comment: Single source of truth for which engine runs which chain stage. Owned by scripts/agent_launch.py; read by the front-door skills. Change routing HERE, never inline in a SKILL.md.

concurrency._comment: The ONLY stage groups allowed to run in the same turn; every other stage is serial. A group may hold at most one write-access stage, because all stages share one worktree and two writers produce overlapping edits to the same files. agent_launch.py --check enforces that, so adding a second writer here fails CI instead of corrupting a run. See .agents/verification-chain.md section 6.

spec-first.why: Spec errors are the most expensive failure in the chain: a wrong spec produces a wrong MR that passed every gate.

spec-critic.why: Independent grader on a separate quota pool. Never the author of the spec it grades.

build.why: Sonnet 5 is near-Opus on coding/agentic work; xhigh keeps reasoning depth where the code is written.

build-review.why: Breaker role. Advisory so a Codex quota exhaustion cannot stall an unattended chain.

migration-safety.why: Rule-shaped work, but guards the only irreversible mistake in the system. Effort stays high even though the model steps down.

security-audit.why: semgrep/gitleaks/uv audit do the detection; the agent orchestrates and triages.

security-tenant-audit.why: The one genuinely open-ended reasoning task in the chain: org_id leakage the scanners cannot pattern-match.

e2e-playwright.why: Authors browser tests mapped to ACs, so it needs write access.

perf-guardrails.why: Budgets in budgets.json do the measuring; perf_triage.py fuses the findings.

test-author.why: Writes tests and refreshes the test map.

test-evaluator.why: Never grade your own tests. Separate quota pool, and read-only so it cannot 'fix' a test into passing.

ci-gate.why: Reads pass/fail from a deterministic pipeline.

merge-request.why: Synthesis from spec and stage reports that already exist on disk.
